question: Do the frozen DON8/EMA8/VOL8 rules, mapped to daily bars at the same calendar horizons, earn positive net returns as a risk-balanced cross-asset portfolio over 2007-2026, on asset classes the rules were never designed on?
registration_note: Registered 2026-09-26, before any strategy result on this data was computed. Only Yahoo chart availability (GLD from 2004-11-18) was checked. The universe rule, the 8h-to-daily parameter mapping, costs and the primary hypothesis are fixed here. Prior literature (time-series momentum across asset classes) exists and is not new evidence; this tests these specific frozen parameters.
evaluation_rule: run exactly once from a commit containing this file

universe_rule.instruments: US-listed ETFs with inception on or before 2007-01-01, one per exposure, covering equity, government and credit bonds, gold, silver, oil, broad commodities, major currencies and real estate

source.provider: Yahoo Finance chart API v8, daily, split- and dividend-adjusted (OHLC scaled by adjclose/close)
source.bar_stamp: each trading day at 00:00 UTC; weekends and holidays are simply absent

parameter_mapping.rule: 8h bar counts divided by 3 to keep the same calendar horizon; thresholds unchanged

economics.not_modelled: short borrow fees, cash yield on idle capital, ETF dividends only via adjusted prices
economics.portfolio: equal capital across sleeves that have data that day, rebalanced daily

sizing.rationale: across asset classes with 5-80% volatility, equal risk per sleeve is the a-priori choice; +/-1 is reported as secondary

primary.series: inverse-vol-sized combined portfolio daily net return
primary.test: Newey-West t (5 lags) of the mean daily net return

secondary_descriptive: per-strategy and per-asset-class Sharpe and t
correlation of the portfolio's daily returns with SPY
